subject: antlion larva
title: This Insect Keeps Its Sand Trap on the Edge of Collapse

scenes.text: This insect builds a trap that is almost ready to collapse. On purpose.
It's the antlion larva. It digs a cone-shaped pit in dry sand in about 15 minutes.
It hides at the bottom with only its jaws showing, waiting for an ant to slip in.
If the ant climbs, the larva flicks sand at it. Studies show that also keeps the walls steep and unstable.
Then it injects digestive fluid, sucks its prey dry, and tosses the empty husk out of the pit.
It does all this for up to three years, and it has no opening for solid waste. It stores it all.

Would you walk past it?
